fix: Borrow instead of cloning: `let text = if leaf_text { semantic.label.as_deref() } else if is_text_input(semantic.role) { semantic.value.as_deref() } else { None };` and at line 321 replace `let next = text.clone().unwrap_or_default();` with `let next = text.unwrap_or_default();` (the `text.clone()` is redundant; `text` is not used afterwards). `set_text_content(Some(next))` and `current != next` accept &str unchanged.

Skip unchanged work: add `bounds: Rect` (or the four f64 values) to NodeElement, and only rebuild the style string and call set_attribute when the node is new or its bounds differ from the stored value. This removes a format! allocation and a DOM style write per node on every publish, for nodes that did not move.

Replace the membership scan over `listed` (a Vec of JS elements compared with `==`, one JS call per pair, O(children x listed) per changed parent) with a set of ids: build `let listed_ids: HashSet<u64> = node.children.iter().copied().collect();` once, and test each current child by its OWNER_ATTRIBUTE id (`element.get_attribute(OWNER_ATTRIBUTE).and_then(|id| id.parse().ok())`) against `listed_ids`. Keep `listed` only for the append loop below.

Each created node element calls `forget()` on four closures (click, focus, keydown, keyup; lines 455, 463, 469), so every node created during the session leaks its closures for the page lifetime even after the element is removed. Store the closures in NodeElement (e.g. `listeners: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>>`, keyboard ones as their own type) and, when a node is removed (the `update.removed` loop and the replace path), remove the listeners from the element first and then drop the closures. Keep the element-owned closures alive for as long as the element is attached.

`tag_name()` converts a JS string into a new Rust String for every existing node on every publish. Store the tag (`tag: &'static str`, as returned by element_kind) in NodeElement and compare `existing.tag == tag` instead.
